segments.text: Episode eighteen. Next stop... the Milky Way.
Our galaxy, the Milky Way, is a giant spiral of stars, gas and dust. We live in one of its arms.
segments.headline: We live in a spiral arm

segments.text: It holds between one hundred and four hundred billion stars.
It's about a hundred thousand light-years across.
No one has ever photographed it from outside. Every picture of the whole galaxy is an illustration, based on maps of its stars.
segments.headline: No photo from outside exists

segments.text: On a dark night, that band of light across the sky is our galaxy, seen from the inside.
segments.headline: Seen from the inside

segments.text: And it isn't alone. Smaller galaxies, like the Magellanic Clouds, orbit around it.
segments.headline: Galaxies orbiting ours

segments.text: Tomorrow, we visit our biggest neighbor, and ask: will it crash into us? Next stop: Andromeda. Follow, so you don't miss episode nineteen.
